items.title: Most users cannot identify AI bias, even in training data
items.raw_excerpt: When recognizing faces and emotions, artificial intelligence (AI) can be biased, like classifying white people as happier than people from other racial backgrounds. This happens because the data used to train the AI contained a disproportionate number of happy white faces, leading it to correlate race with emotional expression. In a recent study, published in Media Psychology, researchers asked users to assess such skewed training data, but most users didn’t notice the bias —

title_i18n.en: Most users cannot identify AI bias, even in training data
title_i18n.zh: 大多数用户无法识别人工智能偏见，即使在训练数据中也是如此。
title_i18n.es: La mayoría de los usuarios no pueden identificar el sesgo de la inteligencia artificial, ni siquiera en los datos de entrenamiento.

excerpt_i18n.en: When recognizing faces and emotions, artificial intelligence (AI) can be biased, like classifying white people as happier than people from other racial backgrounds. This happens because the data used to train the AI contained a disproportionate number of happy white faces, leading it to correlate race with emotional expression. In a recent study, published in Media Psychology, researchers asked users to assess such skewed training data, but most users didn’t notice the bias —
excerpt_i18n.zh: 在识别人脸和情绪时，人工智能可能存在偏见，例如将白人判定为比其他种族背景的人更快乐。这是因为用于训练人工智能的数据存在偏差。
excerpt_i18n.es: Al reconocer rostros y emociones, la inteligencia artificial (IA) puede ser parcial, como clasificar a las personas blancas como más felices que las de otros orígenes raciales. Esto ocurre porque los datos utilizados para entrenar a la IA contienen sesgos.
